cells.Effect: When a sequence outgrows its KV book (a block of KV cache memory for a run of tokens), the scheduler requests a new book. cells.Values and default: Path of a file. The file is opened in append mode with `std::fopen`. Unset: no profile is written. Empty: counts as a path. The open fails and a warning is logged.
cells.Effect: When an allocation from the hugepage heap fails for lack of memory, the arena allocator (`pos_heap_v2`, the build-default allocator of that heap) appends a histogram of the live allocations to this file. The histogram is grouped by size class and by caller address. Each block starts with `=== OOM n_live=`. A profile is written only when the arena allocator is in use and its shadow map (per-allocation tracking) is on: `TRON_HEAP_SHADOW=1` or `--heap-shadow`. The info log line `pos_heap_setup: using arena allocator (pos_heap_v2) with shadow map` confirms both. A failed open logs `heap_v2::dump_profile: could not open`.

hints.suggested: Replace the whole cell with: The arena allocator is `pos_heap_v2`, the build-default allocator of the hugepage heap. An allocation from that heap can fail for lack of memory. The arena allocator then appends a histogram of the live allocations to this file. The histogram is grouped by size class and by caller address. Each block starts with `=== OOM n_live=`. A profile is written only when the arena allocator is in use and its shadow map (per-allocation tracking) is on: `TRON_HEAP_SHADOW=1` or `--heap-shadow`. The info log line `pos_heap_setup: using arena allocator (pos_heap_v2) with shadow map` confirms both. A failed open logs `heap_v2::dump_profile: could not open`.

cells.Values and default: Exactly `1` turns the shadow map on. The code compares the text with `strcmp`. Any other text, such as `true`, is off. No message is logged. Unset: the shadow map is off, unless the option `--heap-shadow` is given.
cells.Effect: Turns on the shadow map of the arena allocator (`pos_heap_v2`, the default allocator for hugepage memory). The shadow map holds one record for each live allocation, with the requested size and 2 caller addresses. Each free checks the pointer and size against the record, and a mismatch aborts the process. `--heap-shadow` does the same, on the command line or in `SYSTEM_CONFIG`. No effect when `TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR` selects the legacy heap. The `TRON_HEAP_PROFILE_PATH` profile of the arena allocator needs the shadow map. Check: the log line `pos_heap_setup: using arena allocator (pos_heap_v2) with shadow map`.

hints.problem: Two names for one allocator. `TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR` says "the legacy allocator" 3 times. `TRON_HEAP_SHADOW` says "the legacy heap". "Legacy allocator" is right, because the heap is the memory and both allocators manage the same heap.
hints.suggested: In `TRON_HEAP_SHADOW`, replace "No effect when `TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR` selects the legacy heap." with "No effect when `TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR` selects the legacy allocator (`pos_heap`)."

cells.Values and default: The exact text `1` selects the arena allocator (`pos_heap_v2`). Any other text selects the legacy allocator (`pos_heap`). That includes `0`, `true` and an empty value. Unset: the build default applies. The CMake option `TRON_ARENA_ALLOCATOR_DEFAULT_ON` is `ON` by default. That selects the arena allocator. Empty: the legacy allocator.
cells.Effect: Selects the allocator of the DMA heap (the hugepage memory that the programs allocate FPGA buffers from). With the arena allocator, KV cache entries are removed when hugepage use passes a target. The FUSE stats files under `/rinzler/stats/dma_heap/` exist only with the arena allocator. No command-line flag selects the allocator. The arena allocator ignores `RZ_KV_CACHE_GB`, `--kv-cache-gb` and `--kv-cache-bytes`, and logs a warning for each one supplied. `TRON_HEAP_SHADOW` needs the arena allocator. Check: the log line `pos_heap_setup: using arena allocator (pos_heap_v2)`. The legacy allocator logs no line.

cells.Values and default: Integer number of queries, parsed with `atoi`. Only a value above `0` is used. Unset: the limit is the value computed for the FPGA card. It is at most 32 queries.
cells.Effect: Lowers the largest number of queries (batch entries) in one hardware attention pass on an FPGA card. The result is the smaller of the value and the limit computed for the card. The variable cannot raise the limit. `0`, a negative number, text that is not a number and an empty value count as unset. There is no error and no log line for the value. The value is read once per process. `rinzler_proxy` does not read it.

cells.Values and default: Integer, parsed with `atoi`. A value above `0` forces the feature on. Every other value forces it off, also text that is not a number. Unset: each FPGA card decides from the project, version and release date of its bitfile. Empty: forces the feature off.
cells.Effect: Forces weight-load reuse for hardware attention on or off for every FPGA card. The bitfile check is skipped. With reuse on, the driver tells the card to reuse its loaded weights when an attention command repeats the weight commands of the previous one. The log shows `HW attention: HWATTN_WLR=<value> forces the feature ON by env flag` (or `OFF`). A forced `ON` is not checked against the bitfile. The log line `bitfile does not support HW attention WLR` ignores the variable. The FUSE stats file `/rinzler/stats/devices/<index>/wcmd_reuse/attn` counts reuse commands.

cells.Read by: libtron, inside `rinzler` and `runtron` (`src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp`). Only a build with the CMake option `TRON_AMX_DISPATCH` reads it.
cells.Values and default: Only the exact text `1` has an effect. Every other text is ignored without a message, for example `0`, `true` or an empty value. Unset: software attention uses the AMX kernel when the CPU, the operating system and the process permission allow AMX.
cells.Effect: With `1`, software attention does not use the AMX kernel (code that uses Intel AMX, a matrix instruction set of the CPU). It uses the AVX-512 code for every KV page. The program reads the value one time, at the first use. `TRON_AMX_DISPATCH` is off by default and on in the `deb` preset (the package build). The AMX kernel serves only models with a head size of 128 dimensions and 4 query heads per KV head. The FUSE stats file `/model/<model id>/attention/summary` shows `amx_available`.
